nodes.summary: The Gaglione–Spellman question (Kourovka 14.32) has a negative answer: it is not the case that every first-order axiomatizable formation of groups is a variety, that is, some class of groups is a formation and is first-order axiomatizable but is not a variety.
nodes.title: Not every axiomatizable formation of groups is a variety

nodes.summary: The proposition that every first-order axiomatizable formation of groups is a variety: every class $\mathfrak{F}$ of groups that is a formation and is first-order axiomatizable is a variety.
nodes.title: The Gaglione–Spellman question on axiomatizable formations (Kourovka 14.32)

nodes.summary: A class of groups, as a predicate on groups in `Type`.
nodes.title: Class of groups

nodes.summary: A class $\mathfrak{F}$ of groups is first-order axiomatizable when there is a theory $T$ in the first-order language of groups such that a group $G$ lies in $\mathfrak{F}$ if and only if $G$, with its canonical structure, is a model of $T$.
nodes.title: First-order axiomatizable classes of groups

nodes.summary: A class $\mathfrak{F}$ of groups is a formation when it contains at least one group, it is closed under surjective homomorphic images (if $G \in \mathfrak{F}$ and $\varphi \colon G \to H$ is a surjective homomorphism, then $H \in \mathfrak{F}$), and for every group $G$ and all normal subgroups $N_1$, $N_2$ of $G$, if $G/N_1$ and $G/N_2$ lie in $\mathfrak{F}$, then so does $G/(N_1 \cap N_2)$.
nodes.title: Formations of groups in the sense of Gaglione and Spellman

nodes.summary: A class $\mathfrak{F}$ of groups is a variety when there is a set $W$ of elements of the free group on generators $x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots$ such that a group $G$ lies in $\mathfrak{F}$ if and only if every $w \in W$ evaluates to $1$ in $G$ under every assignment of elements of $G$ to the generators.
nodes.title: Varieties of groups
